headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: TREK handles secrets and collaborative outputs, while ai-engineering-hub is a docs-only open-source repo with no runtime isolation or verified interaction path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection path is not documented, but TREK uses MCP and real-time collaboration while ai-engineering-hub is an open-source agent repo that may be copied into workflows. With no verified shared channel or parser details, the pairwise prompt-injection risk is limited and uncertain, so I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through a shared MCP server or copied prompts/files, injection becomes plausible.
IF TREK parses ai-engineering-hub content as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the two agents.
Require manual review of copied text before TREK consumes it.
Strip instruction-like markup from imported content.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK clearly touches sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, confirmation numbers, and user accounts, and it writes to local files and logs. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and shows no data classes, but if the pair shares a workspace or TREK uploads file contents, sensitive data could leak. The pathway exists in default collaborative setups, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents share ./data or ./uploads, TREK data can be exposed to the other agent.
IF TREK forwards file contents through its allowlisted egress or MCP, secrets may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Remove secrets from shared files before use.
Disable access to ./data/travel.db and ./uploads for the other agent.
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and shows no write surface, while TREK has collaborative real-time behavior, multiple instances, and writable files. There is no documented lock or coordination between the pair, so if ai-engineering-hub is instantiated into a writable workflow alongside TREK, overlapping writes can conflict. Uncertainty about the first agent's runtime makes medium the safer choice.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub is deployed with filesystem or repo write access, concurrent edits can collide.
IF both agents write to the same TREK files or database without locking, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo or database.
Use a single-writer policy for TREK state.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so it may act on upstream content, while ai-engineering-hub is a source of agent patterns that could be treated as authoritative examples. Because no verification step is documented between them, bad instructions or incorrect facts can cascade into user-facing travel plans or actions. The blast radius is broader than a single document, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF TREK consumes ai-engineering-hub output as guidance without verification, errors can propagate.
IF TREK uses browser or MCP actions based on unreviewed upstream content, downstream mistakes can occur.
mitigations: Require human review before TREK acts on imported guidance.
Mark ai-engineering-hub content as non-authoritative.
Add a verification step before browser or MCP actions.
Limit automated actions to read-only operations.
requires-engineering: implement source-confidence checks and audit trails.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive personal data and secrets, including email addresses, reservations, API keys, and MFA secrets, plus local logs and uploads. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and does not show regulated data handling, so the main compliance concern is TREK's handling of sensitive travel/account data and retention/logging, not a cross-agent residency mismatch. Medium fits because the compliance gap is plausible but not directly evidenced for both agents.
conditions: IF TREK stores secrets or personal data in ./data/logs/trek.log or ./uploads, retention risk increases.
IF the deployment processes EU PII without a matching DPA or residency control, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Review what data is written to logs.
Delete unnecessary uploads and stale records.
Restrict access to secret-bearing files.
Confirm residency and DPA settings before deployment.
requires-engineering: add retention controls and subject-rights workflows.
